tools.title: Tools the AI may use in Feishu
tools.desc: Feishu is a deliberately narrowed venue (a stolen Feishu account is not a stolen computer). These are fixed rules, not settings.
tools.read: Reads (mail / calendar / search / reports / conversation lookup): run without approval.
tools.write: Writes (send, save draft, flag, reschedule…): every call needs a tap on the Feishu approval card; no auto-approve list applies.
tools.connector: External service (MCP) tools: all available; reads run freely, writes always need approval (destructive tools carry a red warning on the card).
tools.web: Web access (search / fetch): controlled by the switch below, off by default; even when on, every call needs approval.
tools.denied: Local commands, file read/write, config and skill changes, and calls out to third-party AI are not registered in Feishu at all — the model cannot see them. Use the desktop app or the remote web app for those.

web.title: Allow web access in Feishu chats
web.desc: Lets the AI search and fetch web pages from Feishu. Off by default: web content is untrusted, and a stolen Feishu account is not a stolen computer. Each call still needs approval.
web.restartHint: Takes effect after restarting the app (the AI engine reads this once at startup).
web.webDisabled: This switch cannot be changed from the remote web app — use the desktop app.

approvals.title: Approvals in Feishu conversations
approvals.desc: The last 10 approve / reject decisions a human actually made. The criterion is "this conversation came from Feishu" — if such a conversation was approved from the desktop app instead, it is still listed here (the record cannot tell which side was tapped). Calls that skipped the card are not counted.
approvals.unavailable: Approval history is unreadable right now (the chat database is not accessible) — this does not mean nothing was ever approved.
approvals.empty: Nothing has been approved or rejected in a Feishu conversation yet.

systemCapabilities.disabledTip: This capability is currently disabled via an environment variable; edit .env and restart the backend to enable it.

The cost: older messages outside the window are invisible at the IMAP layer (history already synced locally is unaffected; this only limits what incremental sync and write operations such as flag / archive can reach). Default 500; set 0 to leave this key entirely to DavMail.

status.error: Failed to write the DavMail config file, so this setting may have no effect: {path} (see the backend log for the reason).
status.disabled: Set to 0: MailAgent leaves this key alone and DavMail uses its own config value (currently {value}).
status.disabledUnset: Set to 0: MailAgent leaves this key alone, and the DavMail config file doesn't set it either (risky on large mailboxes).
